title: Capacity sprint priorities and owner map
summary: Quarterly health/check-in focused on mapping the upcoming capacity sprint, prioritizing items that reduce unit cost at peak, and clarifying owners for reliability improvements. The call surfaced a recent cost spike tied to longer sequence lengths in checkout chat flows and an autoscale configuration that didn't trigger fast enough. Action items were assigned across Redwood (AE/SE) and Harborline teams; next steps include a short pilot for prefix caching, an updated autoscale window, and a tailored pricing note for the committed capacity path.
topics: Usage trends and unexpected token peak
next_steps: Redwood to share short pilot plan for prefix caching and expected savings by 2026-04-27
Harborline SRE to provide recent 72h token length histogram and sample request IDs by 2026-04-25
Redwood SE to propose autoscale window adjustments and smoke test plan by 2026-04-29
action_items: Alicia Park: send tailored committed-capacity pricing example (3-month and 12-month) — due 2026-04-27
Miguel Santos: draft prefix/KV caching pilot steps, required config changes, and rollback plan — due 2026-04-27
Ben Ortiz: export peak-hour traces (IDs + approximate token counts) and share to the shared drive — due 2026-04-25
Samira Khan: confirm internal stakeholders for the sprint and who will own runbook edits — due 2026-04-26
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alicia Park, Miguel Santos, Samira Khan, Ben Ortiz, Lena Moore

Summary block (auto): Quick alignment on capacity sprint priorities; identify owners and immediate pilot to address cost spike.

[00:00] Alicia Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to get through a quick mapping of the capacity sprint priorities today and make sure owners are clear.
[00:28] Samira Khan: yep, thanks Alicia. We've seen two surprise bursts the last week during checkout chat, so main ask is, can we find a quick fix and then a medium term plan.
[01:12] Miguel Santos: quick context from our side, most of the cost impact looks like long context sequences — like 2k+ tokens in some flows — and prefix cache wasn't hitting because the requests aren't consistent enough yet.
[01:40] Ben Ortiz: I dug into the spikes, sorry small crosstalk, the spike aligns with promo launches and a third-party chat widget that appends verbose metadata, so token counts jumped.
[02:05] Alicia Park: got it. are you on hosted or on dedicated for those workloads?
[02:12] Samira Khan: currently hybrid, test traffic is on hosted Redwood API, production on dedicated pools for other models. but this particular chat sits on hosted because of quicker deploy.
[02:41] Miguel Santos: ok so tradeoffs: hosted gives fast turns but cost at peak can be higher; dedicated gives stable throughput if you commit. we should look at short pilot for prefix/KV caching + small autoscale policy change.
[03:08] Lena Moore: from finance side, we need an estimate of unit spend reduction before committing to any long term capacity. can you give a ballpark?
[03:28] Alicia Park: yes we will do a tailored example for 3 and 12 month commits with expected token reductions post-pilot.
[03:46] Samira Khan: also we have auditors asking about logs retention and SOC 2 evidence, so any changes to routing or caching need to maintain auditability.
[04:10] Miguel Santos: completely; we keep audit logs for routing and model variants, and the private deployments have KMS integration — though I'll double check the exact retention export process, sometimes the doc refers to "KV cash" in transcriptions, sorry mis-said, I mean KV cache.
[04:37] Ben Ortiz: (laughs) noted.
[05:05] Alicia Park: can we step through a proposed pilot? Miguel?
[05:12] Miguel Santos: Sure: 1) enable prefix caching on the hosted model variant for the checkout flow for a 48h pilot — will cache common opening sequences; 2) shorten autoscale down-delay from 5 to 2 minutes and raise scale-up aggressiveness threshold; 3) measure P95 latency and token counts during the pilot; 4) revert if error rate > 1.5%.
[05:55] Samira Khan: curious — do we need any code changes on our widget?
[06:02] Miguel Santos: ideally we add a small middleware to strip non-essential metadata before it hits the model. that's optional but it amplifies the savings.
[06:16] Ben Ortiz: we can do that, should be a small change. I'll add that to CI.
[06:30] Lena Moore: what about pricing during the pilot? we pay normal hosted rates?
[06:36] Alicia Park: yes pilot uses existing hosted billing; for committed capacity we'll propose a blended committed price. I'll send examples.
[07:02] Samira Khan: timeline — we'd like a quick win in the next two weeks, then plan the sprint owners for May.
[07:18] Alicia Park: good, so target pilot start 2026-04-28, run 48 hours, then review on 2026-04-30.
[07:28] Ben Ortiz: ok that fits.
[08:00] Miguel Santos: technical note: because the checkout model uses a long KV cache, we need to ensure the cache TTL and shard settings are compatible with the dedicated pools — sometimes kernel selection differs on the dedicated runtime. we may see slight perf delta.
[08:28] Samira Khan: will that affect SLAs? customers expect sub-600ms on checkout.
[08:35] Miguel Santos: we aim for same SLO; but if dedicated kernels are tuned differently you might see +20-30ms, which we think is acceptable, but we'll verify.
[09:05] Alicia Park: let's log that as a risk item.
[09:12] Samira Khan: on compliance, our security lead asked about SSO changes and audit export when you move routes to dedicated — is that straightforward?
[09:28] Miguel Santos: yes, SSO (SAML) and audit logs are supported; for private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key material. I will double-check who owns the config steps.
[09:50] Ben Ortiz: one more operational ask: can we get a list of recommended autoscale settings for bursty e-commerce patterns?
[10:00] Miguel Santos: yes, we'll share a recommended policy: faster scale-up, conservative scale-down, and a warm pool for expected promotion windows.
[10:18] Alicia Park: ok I'm going to map owners now — Ben, you'll own the widget change and trace export; Samira you'll own stakeholder confirmation; Miguel will own the pilot config and rollback play; Alicia will own pricing and exec communications; Lena will sign off on finance acceptance once sample numbers are in.
[10:45] Samira Khan: agreed.
[11:05] Miguel Santos: quick Q from my side — do you want us to run a short benchmark comparing hosted vs dedicated under the same token-length distribution? I can run that if you want.
[11:20] Ben Ortiz: yes please, especially compare P95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[11:28] Alicia Park: add that as a deliverable — Miguel to run benchmark and share results.
[11:40] Lena Moore: and include a simple TCO calc so finance can see breakeven for committed capacity.
[12:00] Alicia Park: will do.
[12:20] Samira Khan: one last ask — can we get a short doc on rollback steps if the prefix cache causes an unexpected regression? we need explicit steps.
[12:30] Miguel Santos: yes we'll include rollback steps in the pilot runbook.
[12:40] Ben Ortiz: rough acceptance criteria for the pilot?
[12:45] Miguel Santos: target >= 12% unit cost reduction and no more than 0.5% error-rate delta; P95 latency should not increase more than 50ms.
[13:05] Alicia Park: fine.
[13:35] Samira Khan: ok, anything else?
[13:45] Lena Moore: no, just please include finance numbers early.
[14:00] Alicia Park: recap and next steps: Redwood to share pilot plan and pricing examples by 2026-04-27; Harborline to send traces and confirm owners by 2026-04-26; starting pilot 2026-04-28.
[14:30] Ben Ortiz: confirmed.
[14:40] Miguel Santos: I'll put the pilot steps into the shared folder and tag the runbook.
[15:00] Samira Khan: thanks everyone.

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cash"), timestamps are approximate, filler words preserved. End of transcript.
